description: The op-4542 Wakao exponent fix landed in tuas_boussinesq_solver on 2026-08-11 (WakaoData::get() now computes the published Nu = 2 + 1.1 Pr^(1/3) Re^0.6). crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/mod.rs still describes the TUAS defect as 'Warning, still current', and crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/cht.rs says 'Do not unify the two until op-4542 is closed' and carries a divergence_from_the_tuas_wakao_implementation test pinning the ~5.8x divergence (independently reproduced: 5.8475 at Re=1000, Pr=0.7). Once op-4542 is closed by the maintainer, these warnings and the divergence test need updating (the divergence test will presumably now FAIL or need repurposing since the two implementations agree). NOT fixed during the op-4542 fleet because a sibling fleet was live in crates/tampines/ -- deliberately left to the tampines owners. Blocked on maintainer closing op-4542.
title: tampines: pebble_bed cht.rs/mod.rs carry now-stale 'TUAS Wakao defect still current' warnings after op-4542 fix

description:
Found 2026-08-22 wiring op-l3uz's def/sig/refs: RustAnalyzerSession::connect_with_observed spawns a FRESH rust-analyzer and waits out the full index (up to KOVAN_RA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 180s default) on EVERY kovan-cli def/sig/refs invocation, then shuts it down -- no session reuse across separate CLI processes. Fine for a single one-shot query, wasteful for an agent making several in a session.

kopitiam-semantic already ships the right primitive for a long-lived host: AsyncRustAnalyzerSession (crates/kopitiam-semantic/src/async_session.rs) -- spawn_async() returns immediately, state()/is_ready() poll non-blockingly (LspState::Connecting/Ready/Failed), and definition/references/hover/rename/code_actions/apply_code_action all return RequestError::NotReady{state} instead of blocking. This is built for exactly a background-indexing daemon, not a one-shot CLI call.

PROPOSED SHAPE (not yet built, needs a design decision before implementation):
- A 'kovan-cli lsp-daemon' background process hosting one AsyncRustAnalyzerSession per (root, rust-analyzer) pair, listening on a local IPC channel. kovan-cli def/sig/refs (and the not-yet-built rename/code-actions, op-<rename-bead>) become thin clients: check for a live daemon, use it if present, else fall back to today's spawn-per-call path (never a hard dependency on the daemon existing).
- Precedent already dogfooded in this exact workspace: kopi-beans' own 'bn daemon run' (confirmed running via ps aux, 2026-08-22) -- same lazy-spawn / long-lived-background-process shape, so this is not a novel pattern here.
- Lazy spawn on first use, idle-timeout auto-shutdown (e.g. 10-15 min of no requests) so it does not linger forever or need explicit start/stop.
- IPC choice needs a decision: a Unix domain socket is the natural choice on Linux/Termux, but Windows has no Unix sockets (named pipes there) -- this workspace's Android/Windows-portability discipline (CLAUDE.md) means the IPC layer needs a cross-platform answer or an explicit Windows fallback (spawn-per-call, no daemon) before this ships, not an unstated gap.
- Alternative/complementary: kovan-tui, when a human has it open, is ALREADY a long-running process -- it could host the same daemon role, with kovan-cli preferring it if reachable. Doesn't help an agent-only session where nothing keeps kovan-tui open, so the standalone daemon is still needed as the primary path.
title: kovan-cli: DESIGN -- keep rust-analyzer warm across invocations (daemon, avoid per-call cold-start)
